title: Quality tier
summary: Scores AI-generated artifacts against production quality controls before sensitive enforcement or transport runs.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Quality tier AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Quality tier Scores AI-generated artifacts against production quality controls before sensitive enforcement or transport runs. The Quality tier is the first gate in the fence flow. It scores an AI-generated artifact and decides whether it is fit to proceed. A failing artifact is stopped before Guard evaluates the action. # Architecture text Copy quality/source/control_registry.csv   ~1,000 canonical controls
        │
        ▼
aifence.quality.controls              loader, capability lookup
        │
        ▼
aifence.quality.gate                  the in-process gate The canonical quality-control pack lives under the repository's top-level quality/ directory. The Python package aifence.quality is a bridge that reads the control registry and runs a fast deterministic gate in process. # Checks | Check | Weight | Mandatory | What it catches |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| completeness | 40 | yes | An empty artifact. |
| anti_template | 25 | yes | Unresolved TODO , TBD , PLACEHOLDER , Lorem ipsum . |
| answerability | 15 | no | Too little substance to be useful. |
| link_integrity | 10 | no | Empty or placeholder links in markup. |
| structure | 10 | no | Missing headings or landmarks in markup. |
| json_validity | 35 | yes | JSON artifacts that do not parse. |
| schema_conformance | 25 | yes | Output violating a supplied JSON Schema. |
| grounding | 20 | conditional | Numeric claims absent from supplied sources. | # Outcomes accept — score meets the threshold and no mandatory check failed. revise — no mandatory failure, but the score is below min_score . reject — a mandatory check failed. Score is irrelevant. This is why an artifact can score well and still be rejected: a single unresolved placeholder is disqualifying. # Schema conformance With the quality extra installed, full JSON Schema validation applies. Without it, the gate falls back to a required-property and type subset so a missing contract field is still caught rather than silently passing. # Grounding Given sources , the gate reports numeric claims in the artifact that appear nowhere in the source material. One unsourced figure is a warning; a cluster of more than two fails the gate outright. json Copy // sources say 4.2M / 12% / 1500 accounts
"Revenue reached 9.9 million, up 87 percent, across 4200 accounts…"
// → grounding: 4 numeric claim(s) absent from sources → reject # API | Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| GET /v1/quality/registry | Summary of the loaded control registry. |
| GET /v1/quality/controls | List controls, filterable by priority. |
| POST /v1/quality/evaluate | Run the gate over an artifact. | View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. On this page Architecture Checks Outcomes Schema conformance Grounding API

title: Deployment
summary: Migrations, containers, Helm, production hardening, multi-region active/standby topology, and broker transports.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Deployment AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Deployment Migrations, containers, Helm, production hardening, multi-region active/standby topology, and broker transports. # Database migrations Production should run with AIFENCE_AUTO_CREATE_SCHEMA=false ; Alembic is the only thing that creates tables. bash Copy alembic upgrade head A test asserts migrations produce the declared models and the history has one head, preventing silent schema drift. # Container bash Copy docker compose up --build      # PostgreSQL + the control plane The image runs as a non-root user and serves aifence-api on port 8080. # Helm The chart lives under deploy/helm/aifence and deploys the control plane plus dispatcher, lifecycle and audit-anchor worker roles, migration job, network policy, HPA, PDB and ingress. bash Copy helm upgrade --install aifence deploy/helm/aifence -f my-values.yaml # Production validation Production refuses to start without the configured hardening requirements, including verified TLS for PostgreSQL, mTLS, external KMS/non-exportable signing, durable evidence storage, independent audit anchoring, controlled egress and workload identity. # Multi-region topology Exactly one region is active : it owns the writable database and durable workers. Other regions are standby : they can serve the control plane from replicas and remain warm for promotion. yaml Copy # active
region: { name: eu-west-1, role: active }
# standby
region: { name: us-east-1, role: standby } Three independent guardrails prevent a standby from behaving like the active region: Startup validation refuses standby + durable worker role. The Helm chart does not render durable workers/migration outside the active region. Readiness publishes accepts_writes , so a global load balancer sends writes only to active. # Bus transports bash Copy AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT=redis
AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_TOPIC=aifence.handoffs Publication happens after the durable commit and carries routing identity rather than semantic content. # Health and observability | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| /health/live | Liveness probe. |
| /health/ready | Readiness; reports region and accepts_writes . |
| /metrics | Prometheus scrape target. | Set AIFENCE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to enable OpenTelemetry tracing. View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. On this page Database migrations Container Helm Production validation Multi-region topology Bus transports Health and observability

title: Benchmarks
summary: AIFENCE tracks hostile behavior caught and legitimate work disrupted together. Either number alone can hide an unusable policy.
text: Benchmarks / measured regressions Measure detection. Measure friction. AIFENCE tracks hostile behavior caught and legitimate work disrupted together. Either number alone can hide an unusable policy. TRACE CORPUS 18 11 attack · 7 benign BEHAVIORAL DETECTION 100% measured overall FALSE POSITIVE 0% hard-refusal rate BALANCED HOLD 14.3% vs 71.4% strict Policy profiles Security outcome and approval friction. On the measured 18-trace regression corpus, behavioral analysis enables the balanced profile to preserve the measured detection outcome while reducing held benign traces. Strict 100% measured detection / 0% measured hard false positives / 71.4% benign hold. Balanced + behavioral 100% measured detection / 0% measured hard false positives / 14.3% benign hold. Important limitation 18 traces are useful regression evidence and far too small to represent population-level safety guarantees. MEASURED VISUALS Regression evidence, without dashboard noise. Latency is environment-specific regression evidence. Detection and approval-friction results describe the measured trace corpus, not population-level guarantees. COMPOSED FENCE Latency distribution markers POLICY PROFILES Detection and hold rate

title: Bus tier
summary: The semantic communication runtime — durable handoffs, content-addressed references, learned patterns, and minimum-sufficient state.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Bus tier AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Bus tier The semantic communication runtime — durable handoffs, content-addressed references, learned patterns, and minimum-sufficient state. The Bus tier is a vendor-neutral semantic communication runtime. It carries the minimum state a downstream agent needs rather than resending whole conversations: content-addressed references, immutable deltas, learned compositional patterns, provenance, and a model of what the receiver already knows. # Durable delivery text Copy handoff ──▶ pending ──▶ claimed ──▶ acknowledged
                          │
                          └─▶ lease expiry ──▶ claimable again A handoff is committed to the database before it is considered delivered. Receiver knowledge advances only after acknowledgement, so a claimed but unacked message is redelivered rather than lost. # Semantic compression The bus compresses meaning rather than bytes. Negation, amounts, identities, authorization, deadlines, environment markers, instructions and constraints take the strict preservation path. Unknown or ambiguous meaning remains literal or referenced. # Learned patterns Recurring semantic structures move through candidate, shadow validation and counterfactual evaluation before becoming active. Promotion accounts for frequency, savings, stability, ambiguity, source trust/diversity, holdout evidence and receiver-specific fidelity. # Content-addressed references Stored content uses SHA-256 identity. Authorization and lifetime are separate grants, so identical bytes deduplicate without sharing authorization. Grants support workspace/owner scope, agent ACLs, field paths, memory tier, TTL, provenance and optional AES-GCM encryption at rest. # Broker transports | Backend | Mechanism | Extra |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none | No fan-out (default) | — |
| memory | In-process, for tests | — |
| redis | Redis Stream ( XADD ) | redis |
| kafka | Topic keyed by receiver | kafka |
| rabbitmq | Durable topic exchange | rabbitmq | Publication follows the durable commit, and events carry identity/routing metadata rather than semantic content. A broker outage is reported in the receipt instead of being converted into a false success. # Protocol and conformance The bus reads and writes sage/0.2 , wire version 2. Protocol identity is canonical MessagePack plus SHA-256; JSON is the readable representation. A language-neutral conformance kit of 13 normative vectors (6 valid, 7 invalid) is consumed independently by Python, JavaScript and Go implementations. View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. On this page Durable delivery Semantic compression Learned patterns Content-addressed references Broker transports Protocol and conformance

title: Architecture
summary: AIFENCE composes Quality, Guard, and Bus into one FastAPI application with shared identity, database, audit correlation, telemetry, and lifecycle—without collapsing their domain responsibilities.
text:
Architecture / one composed control plane Shared foundation. Independent contracts. AIFENCE composes Quality, Guard, and Bus into one FastAPI application with shared identity, database, audit correlation, telemetry, and lifecycle—without collapsing their domain responsibilities. aifence.core Shared configuration, database Base/engine, middleware, errors, metrics, telemetry, request identity, and environment helpers. Quality Native root router and deterministic admission evaluator plus explicit Deep Quality bridge. Guard Mounted enforcement sub-application, shared DB/identity, policy/capability/audit internals. Bus Mounted semantic transport with durable DB source-of-truth and optional broker fan-out. One migration history Every subsystem model shares the same declarative Base and Alembic history; migration/model drift is tested. Composition seam Register, don’t hard-wire. aifence.app.create_app()
  ├─ core middleware / identity / metrics / OpenAPI
  ├─ quality.register(app, ctx)
  ├─ guard.register(app, ctx)
  └─ bus.register(app, ctx)

POST /v1/fence/submit
  → Quality admission
  → Guard enforcement
  → durable Bus handoff
  → fence.completed audit

title: Fence flow
summary: The three tiers as one governed pipeline, with short-circuiting, resilience budgets, and one truthful receipt.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Fence flow AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Fence flow The three tiers as one governed pipeline, with short-circuiting, resilience budgets, and one truthful receipt. The fence flow is what makes AIFENCE one system rather than three services sharing a host. A single authenticated request runs through all three tiers in process and returns one receipt describing what each tier decided. text Copy POST /v1/fence/submit
   │
   ├── quality gate ──── fails ──▶ blocked_by_quality   (guard never runs)
   │        │ passes
   ├── guard enforcement ─ denies ─▶ blocked_by_guard    (bus never runs)
   │        │ allows
   └── durable handoff ─── degraded ─▶ authorized_not_delivered
            │ delivered
            └──────────────────────▶ handed_off # Outcomes | final_outcome | allowed | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| handed_off | true | Passed every tier; a claimable message was persisted. |
| blocked_by_quality | false | The artifact failed the quality gate. |
| blocked_by_guard | false | Policy denied or required approval. |
| authorized_not_delivered | true | Permitted, but transport was degraded. | authorized_not_delivered exists so the receipt never claims a handoff that did not happen. # The receipt json Copy {
  "request_id": "req_…",
  "tenant_id": "ten_…",
  "allowed": true,
  "final_outcome": "handed_off",
  "degraded_tiers": [],
  "stages": {
    "quality": { "passed": true, "score": 100 },
    "guard": { "outcome": "allow", "matched_rule": "baseline:read-only-low-risk" },
    "bus": { "delivered": true, "message_id": "M…", "content_ref": "aifence:sha256:…" }
  }
} # Resilience Every tier is fail-closed by default: a tier that cannot answer within its latency budget causes 503 tier_unavailable . Repeated failures trip a circuit breaker and short-circuit the tier for a recovery window. quality and bus may be configured advisory. Guard cannot — naming it as fail-open is rejected at startup. # Grounding a submission Supplying sources enables the quality tier's grounding check for the whole flow, so fabricated figures are stopped before enforcement. # Relationship to the Guard API | Endpoint | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| POST /guard/v1/decisions | You want an enforcement decision only. |
| POST /v1/fence/submit | You want the full pipeline and a durable handoff. | View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. On this page Outcomes The receipt Resilience Grounding a submission Relationship to the Guard API

title: Getting started
summary: Install AIFENCE, mint a key, and run an artifact through the complete Quality → Guard → Bus fence.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Getting started AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Getting started Install AIFENCE, mint a key, and run an artifact through the complete Quality → Guard → Bus fence. # Install AIFENCE targets Python 3.12+. Create an isolated environment and install the repository in editable mode. bash Copy python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
pip install -e ".[dev]" Optional extras include postgres , s3 , mcp , otel , quality (full JSON Schema), redis , kafka , rabbitmq , and bench . # Run bash Copy aifence-api The composed application serves on 0.0.0.0:8080 . In development it can create the schema automatically; in production use migrations. bash Copy curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health/ready json Copy { "ready": true,
  "subsystems": ["aifence.quality","aifence.guard","aifence.bus"],
  "region_role": "active",
  "accepts_writes": true } # Create a tenant and API key Every authenticated surface uses guard-issued keys. Bootstrap the first tenant and administrative key: bash Copy python -c "
from aifence.app import create_app
from aifence.core.config import CoreSettings
app = create_app(CoreSettings())
with app.state.session_factory() as s:
    _t, _k, secret = app.state.guard_app.state.service.create_tenant_and_key(
        s, tenant_name='Example Org', key_name='bootstrap', scopes=['*'])
print(secret)
" The secret is printed once. Store it in a secret manager immediately. # Run an artifact through the fence bash Copy curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/fence/submit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AIFENCE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "artifact": "# Q3 Report\n\nRevenue grew 12% to $4.2M across all regions.",
    "content_type": "text/markdown",
    "receiver": "analytics-agent",
    "action": { "operation": "read" }
  }' A successful run returns final_outcome: "handed_off" and a durable message_id the receiver can claim from the bus. # Watch it block Placeholders fail the quality gate before enforcement runs: bash Copy -d '{"artifact": "# Draft\n\nTODO: write this.", "content_type": "text/markdown"}'
# → blocked_by_quality A destructive, high-risk action can pass quality but be stopped by Guard: bash Copy -d '{"artifact": "…", "action": {"operation": "delete", "destructive": true},
     "risk_score": 80}'
# → blocked_by_guard # Next steps Fence flow — outcomes and the receipt format. Configuration — the environment surface and fail-closed settings. SDKs — Python, TypeScript and Go clients with framework hooks. Deployment — migrations, Helm and multi-region topology. View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. title: Failure semantics
summary: Failure behavior is part of the AIFENCE security contract, not an incidental runtime detail.
text: DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Version model Core tiers Quality Quality modes Guard Bus Bus protocol Reference API reference Configuration Architecture SDKs Assurance Benchmarks Security model Threat model Failure semantics Supply chain Operations Deployment Operations AIFENCE / Docs / Failure semantics AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Failure semantics Failure behavior is part of the AIFENCE security contract, not an incidental runtime detail. # Default behavior Component / failure Default Reason Quality admission timeout/unavailable Fail closed Unvetted artifacts do not silently proceed Guard timeout/unavailable/policy error Always fail closed Authorization never degrades into authorization-by-absence Bus persistence/handoff failure Fail closed A receipt cannot claim a handoff that was not committed Fence audit append failure Fail closed A governed decision without its audit event is incomplete Optional telemetry exporter failure Degraded Telemetry transport is not an authorization dependency Optional broker fan-out failure Degraded / retry Database-backed Bus remains source of truth Database unavailable Fail closed Identity, policy, audit and handoff state are unavailable Signing/KMS unavailable Fail closed where signed evidence is required Unsigned evidence cannot be represented as verified Deep Quality runtime unavailable Admission remains available Deep evaluation is explicit, not an admission dependency # Narrow fail-open exception Only quality and bus may be deliberately named as advisory fence tiers. guard is rejected if present in AIFENCE_FLOW_FAIL_OPEN_TIERS . # Receipt rule A handed_off receipt means admission passed, Guard permitted the action, the Bus handoff was durably created, and the fence-completion audit event was appended. Optional telemetry export and broker propagation are not part of that transactional success claim. View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. title: Developers
summary: Start with the composed demo, inspect the OpenAPI surface, then use Python, TypeScript, or Go clients against explicit AIFENCE outcomes.

title: How it works
summary: The composed fence takes one authenticated request through artifact admission, mandatory authorization, durable delivery, and completion evidence.
text: How it works / one governed transaction Intent becomes an explicit outcome. The composed fence takes one authenticated request through artifact admission, mandatory authorization, durable delivery, and completion evidence. Run the interactive simulation 01 · Authenticate Resolve the caller into the same Guard-backed identity model used by the fence and governed endpoints. 02 · Admit Quality emits explicit mode/profile metadata and stable finding IDs. 03 · Enforce Guard compiles policy into an enforcement decision and exact-action capability. Errors fail closed. 04 · Persist Bus creates a tenant-scoped handoff before broker fan-out or delivery claims. 05 · Evidence The completion event appends stage truth, request identity, hashes, and signing identity into the audit path. Failure semantics A failure is part of the contract. blocked_by_quality Artifact admission failed; Guard and Bus are not falsely represented as completed. blocked_by_guard Policy denied or held the action. Bus does not create a governed handoff. unavailable Required persistence/evidence failed. Authorization never turns into a false delivery receipt.

title: The governed boundary for AI agents
summary: Not another agent framework. Not another prompt filter. AIFENCE governs the path from generated work to authorized, durable, auditable execution.
text: UNCONTROLLED SCENE 00 / 05 REQUEST req_8A41 TENANT acme RENDER AUTO 00 01 02 03 04 05 GUIDED INSPECT SKIP agent intent AQ-COMPLETE-001 exact-action capability tenant handoff signed evidence 00 / OUTSIDE THE BOUNDARY Every agent will act. The question is what happens before generated intent becomes a real tool call, write, transfer, or handoff. Enter AIFENCE Run a scenario 01 / THE FENCE Capability is not authority. AIFENCE creates a governed execution boundary between agent intent and downstream action. Identity, artifact quality, policy, delivery state, and evidence become explicit before success can be claimed. BEFORE unverified AFTER governed path AUTHORITY agent-claimed AUTHORITY externalized 02 / QUALITY INSPECTION Should this work proceed? The artifact enters a clinical inspection chamber. Deterministic admission checks look for completeness, unresolved templates, structure, grounding, JSON validity, and schema obligations. MODE admission AQ-COMPLETE-001 PASS AQ-TEMPLATE-001 PASS ADMISSION PASS 03 / GUARD AUTHORIZATION VAULT May this agent do this? Identity, tenant, operation, resource, arguments, environment, risk, and policy converge on one mandatory fail-closed decision. Allowance becomes a narrow exact-action capability—not general permission. PRINCIPAL agent:release TENANT acme OPERATION read MATCHED RULE GUARD_ALLOW 04 / BUS TRANSPORT INFRASTRUCTURE Authorized is not delivered. Bus commits a tenant-scoped semantic handoff before delivery can be represented as successful. Claims are leased, acknowledgements advance state, and tenant lanes never collapse into one another. WORKSPACE tenant:acme PERSISTENCE COMMITTED STATE claimed FINAL acknowledged 05 / EVIDENCE ROOM Chaos entered. Evidence came out. Quality passed. Guard allowed. Bus committed. Audit appended. The receipt is a compact statement of what actually happened. AIFENCE RECEIPT / req_8A41 tenant / acme QUALITY PASS GUARD ALLOW BUS HANDED_OFF AUDIT #42 SIGNED event_hash sha256:92df…08c1 · signing_key_id ed25519:31a7…6f2c Run another scenario Inspect assurance THE CONTROL BOUNDARY AIFENCE sits in between. Not another agent framework. Not another prompt filter. AIFENCE governs the path from generated work to authorized, durable, auditable execution. WITHOUT AIFENCE Intent collapses into action. agent output looks plausible tool call self-authorized handoff best effort success ambiguous WITH AIFENCE Each claim becomes explicit. Quality admitted Guard authorized Bus committed receipt evidenced INTERACTIVE FENCE SIMULATOR Change the request. Watch the boundary react. Safe read, destructive write, incomplete artifact, cross-tenant request, Bus persistence failure, or changed-content replay. Downstream stages stop when upstream truth fails. INPUT / SCENARIO SAFE READ PRIVILEGED WRITE INCOMPLETE CROSS-TENANT BUS FAILURE CHANGED REPLAY Artifact Operation read write delete Tenant Receiver Submit through fence EXECUTION / LIVE STATE 01 QUALITY READY admission 02 GUARD WAITING mandatory 03 BUS WAITING durable 04 AUDIT WAITING append Request ready. Submit to execute the governed path. request_id — allowed — final_outcome — evidence receipt appears after execution FOUR CONTRACTS One boundary. Different responsibilities. The visual grammar stays consistent with the tour: inspection for Quality, constrained authority for Guard, isolated infrastructure for Bus, and a sealed chain for evidence. 01 Quality / Admission Deterministic artifact admission before sensitive authorization begins. 02 Guard / Enforcement Mandatory fail-closed policy outside the agent process, bound to an exact action. 03 Bus / Handoff Durable, tenant-scoped semantic transport with truthful delivery state. 04 Evidence / Audit Correlation identity, event hash, sequence, and signing key evidence. EXECUTED ASSURANCE Proof, not adjectives. The verified pre-tag tree has a deep assurance layer spanning tests, coverage, fuzzing, mutation, compatibility, reproducibility, SBOM generation, and container scanning. PYTHON SUITE 608 passed LINE COVERAGE 83.29% independent gate BRANCH COVERAGE 64.52% independent gate WIRE FUZZ 5000 / 5000 BUS TCK 13/13 Python · JS · Go ASSURANCE PROFILE Coverage against policy floors BEHAVIORAL REGRESSION Detection vs approval friction Open assurance ledger View benchmark detail WHO BENEFITS One execution path. Four operational views. Security, platform, AI engineering, and governance teams can reason about the same event without relying on the agent’s own narrative. SECURITY Policy outside the model. Fail-closed enforcement, stable reason codes, tenant boundaries, and exact-action capabilities. PLATFORM Durable state instead of best effort. One composed control plane, PostgreSQL-backed truth, broker compatibility, and explicit degradation. AI ENGINEERING Machine-readable outcomes. Deterministic AQ findings, structured errors, SDKs, and a canonical composed endpoint. AUDIT Evidence instead of screenshots. Correlation identity, signed receipts, hash-linked events, SBOMs, and certified artifacts. PLACEMENT What AIFENCE is. What it is not. AIFENCE is a governed action boundary. It complements IAM, secrets management, model safety, SIEM, and downstream application controls. Between Agent/application intent and sensitive downstream execution. Owns Artifact admission, externalized enforcement, durable semantic handoff, and correlation/audit evidence. Integrates with PostgreSQL, Redis/Kafka/RabbitMQ, OpenTelemetry, KMS/signing, SDKs, MCP, Helm, and agent adapters. Does not replace Infrastructure IAM, model alignment, human review programs, downstream authorization, or incident response. ENTER THE PRODUCT Govern the action path, not just the prompt. title: Guard tier
summary: The enforcement plane — decides and enforces what an agent is permitted to do.
text:
DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Core tiers Quality Guard Bus Reference API reference Configuration Architecture Assurance Benchmarks Security model Operations Deployment Operations SDKs AIFENCE / Docs / Guard tier AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Guard tier The enforcement plane — decides and enforces what an agent is permitted to do. The Guard tier sits outside the agent process and evaluates every sensitive action before it reaches a provider, tool, data source, artifact store, or another agent. Required controls must compile into an executable enforcement plan or the operation fails closed. # Decision pipeline text Copy DecisionRequest
   │
   ├─▶ detectors ──────▶ findings (category, severity, confidence)
   │                        │
   ├─▶ content classifier ──┤   observed data classes
   │                        ▼
   ├─▶ risk scoring ─────▶ risk 0–100
   │                        │
   └─▶ policy engine ───────┴─▶ outcome + constraints
                                     │
                                     ▼
                            enforcement plan → capability token # Outcomes | Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| allow | Proceed unchanged. |
| allow_with_limits | Proceed under constraints. |
| redact_or_transform | Proceed only after transformation. |
| require_approval | Hold for a human decision. |
| deny | Refuse. |
| quarantine_and_terminate | Refuse, isolate the artifact, and end the run. | # Detectors Stable finding categories include prompt injection, data exfiltration, secret exposure, undeclared sensitive content, control evasion, instruction drift, material misrepresentation, fabricated completion, scope violations, disallowed tools, dangerous commands, and excessive delegation depth. # Capability tokens An allowed decision does not itself perform the action. Guard issues an exact-action capability token bound to the tool, operation, resource and arguments, with a TTL and maximum use count. A token obtained for one action cannot be replayed against another. # Identity and access Tenants isolate data with PostgreSQL row-level security. API keys are scoped and can be bound to an immutable agent manifest, workload, instance and principal. Workload identity can be provided through trusted SPIFFE assertions from a mutually authenticated proxy. # Evidence Every decision produces a signed receipt and events are written to a hash-chained audit log with periodic checkpoints. Checkpoints can be anchored to independently administered external destinations. # Worker roles Guard separates control-plane , dispatcher , lifecycle , anchor , migration , and maintenance runtime roles so durable work can scale independently. # Production posture Production validation refuses to start without the configured hardening requirements: PostgreSQL/TLS, mTLS, non-exportable signing, external KMS, durable evidence storage, independent audit anchoring, controlled egress, and workload identity. View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. title: Security
summary: AIFENCE moves sensitive authorization outside the agent process, binds policy to tenant and exact action, and keeps required control failures fail-closed.
text: Security / externalized authority Agents propose. Guard decides. AIFENCE moves sensitive authorization outside the agent process, binds policy to tenant and exact action, and keeps required control failures fail-closed. Threat model Failure semantics Fail closed Guard cannot fail open. Required database, audit, signing, and policy failures preserve denial rather than inventing authority. Tenant boundaries Identity and Bus workspaces remain tenant-scoped; knowing a receiver or message identifier does not grant cross-tenant access. Exact action Capabilities can bind tool, operation, resource, arguments, TTL, and usage rather than granting broad ambient permission. Priority threats Regression-backed boundaries. AIFENCE maps security objectives to explicit controls and tests rather than relying on a generic “agent safety” claim. Confused deputy Mandatory Guard stage + exact-action capabilities. Cross-tenant access Tenant-scoped identity, storage, and Bus workspaces. Replay with changed content Idempotency binds sender, receiver, and payload digest. Tampered wire Frozen wire v2 schema and shared cross-language TCK. Audit tampering Per-tenant hash-chain/signing evidence and independently anchorable checkpoints.

title: Threat model
summary: Trust boundaries and regression-backed controls for unauthorized, unaudited, cross-tenant, or tampered agent actions and handoffs.
text: DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Version model Core tiers Quality Quality modes Guard Bus Bus protocol Reference API reference Configuration Architecture SDKs Assurance Benchmarks Security model Threat model Failure semantics Supply chain Operations Deployment Operations AIFENCE / Docs / Threat model AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Threat model Trust boundaries and regression-backed controls for unauthorized, unaudited, cross-tenant, or tampered agent actions and handoffs. # Security objective AIFENCE prevents an AI agent or integration from converting untrusted/generated work into an unauthorized or unaudited downstream action, and prevents semantic handoff state from crossing tenant or protocol boundaries without enforcement. # Trust boundaries Caller → composed API: API keys/mTLS establish identity; request-size and host/origin controls constrain ingress. Quality → Guard: admission quality never grants authority; Guard independently evaluates action, principal, environment and risk. Guard → Bus: only permitted Guard outcomes can create a fence handoff. Tenant → tenant: Bus workspaces and identity state are tenant-scoped. Wire → implementation: Bus wire v2 is validated against the frozen protocol/TCK contract. Runtime → evidence: audit events are hash-chained and signed without copying artifact contents into fence-completion events. # Priority threats Threat Primary control Coverage Anonymous fence use Shared Guard-backed identity Fence conformance Cross-tenant message access Tenant-specific Bus workspace Fence conformance Policy bypass / confused deputy Mandatory fail-closed Guard stage Integration + red-team Ambiguous denial handling Stable Guard reason codes + matched rule Guard policy/service tests Low-quality placeholder work Stable Admission Quality findings Quality/fence tests Idempotency replay with changed content Sender/receiver/payload digest binding Bus + conformance Malformed/tampered semantic wire Frozen schema + TCK + mutation suite Bus conformance Audit tampering Per-tenant hash chain + signatures/checkpoints Audit + fence conformance Oversized request abuse Streaming-aware request limiter Core/integration Unsafe production defaults Startup validation Configuration tests Secret leakage through metrics Private metrics + bearer auth Core application tests Source/package drift Release/registry/package gates CI release checks # Residual risk AIFENCE cannot prove that external tools, models or downstream agents behave correctly after authorized execution. Operators still need to protect infrastructure credentials, configure tenant policy correctly, secure database/KMS infrastructure, and evaluate model-specific prompt/tool risks. title: Bus protocol
summary: Cross-language semantic handoff compatibility is governed by aifence/0.2, wire version 2, and a shared conformance kit.
text: DOCUMENTATION ⌕ Search documentation... ⌘ K Overview Getting started Fence flow Version model Core tiers Quality Quality modes Guard Bus Bus protocol Reference API reference Configuration Architecture SDKs Assurance Benchmarks Security model Threat model Failure semantics Supply chain Operations Deployment Operations AIFENCE / Docs / Bus protocol AIFENCE DOCUMENTATION Bus protocol Cross-language semantic handoff compatibility is governed by aifence/0.2, wire version 2, and a shared conformance kit. # Protocol identity The Bus implementation version and wire protocol are separate contracts. Current protocol identity is aifence/0.2 with wire version 2 . # Compatibility rules Every packet is validated as wire v2 before expansion. Canonical JSON, canonical MessagePack and SHA-256 digests must match shared vectors. Invalid vectors must be rejected. Python, JavaScript and Go consume the same central TCK vectors. Adapter-local standalone copies must remain byte-identical to the central vectors. # Change rule Protocol changes require a new protocol/wire version or an explicitly backward-compatible TCK change. Bumping the Bus implementation package alone does not redefine wire compatibility. bash Copy python -m aifence.bus.conformance --fuzz View source repository ↗ Documentation snapshot for the governed control plane. title: Product
summary: AIFENCE separates four claims that agent systems often blur together: Is the work good enough? Is the action allowed? Was it durably handed off? Can you prove what happened?
text: Product / governed execution One boundary around agent action. AIFENCE separates four claims that agent systems often blur together: Is the work good enough? Is the action allowed? Was it durably handed off? Can you prove what happened? Take the 3D tour How it works Quality Deterministic admission before downstream authority. Guard Mandatory fail-closed policy outside the agent. Bus Durable tenant-scoped semantic handoff. Evidence One correlation identity and truthful completion receipt. Product contract Quality → Guard → Bus Every tier owns a separate invariant. A downstream success cannot rewrite an upstream failure, and an authorization cannot be represented as delivery before persistence succeeds. Quality Stops incomplete, placeholder, structurally invalid, or insufficiently grounded artifacts before sensitive action evaluation. Guard Evaluates principal, tenant, policy, resource, operation, and risk; cannot be configured fail-open. Bus Commits the approved handoff durably, supports claim/ack and lease recovery, and enforces tenant-scoped workspaces. Receipt Reports handed_off only after the durable handoff and completion audit event actually exist.
